questions.question: What is 어머 doing here?
questions.explanation: 어머 marks the surprise itself — the actual compliment comes right after, in a different sentence.

dialogue.speaker: 친구
dialogue.korean: 나 시험 완전 망친 것 같아...
dialogue.roman: na siheom wanjeon mangchin geot gata...

questions.question: What is 나 doing with 오히려 좋아?
questions.explanation: 오히려 좋아 doesn’t laugh at the bad news — it points at the opportunity hiding inside it.

options.text: Reframing the bad news as an opportunity.
Agreeing that the exam really did go badly.
Offering to help them study next time.

dialogue.speaker: 친구
dialogue.korean: 쟤 또 우리 얘기 하고 다니나 봐.
dialogue.roman: jyae tto uri yaegi hago danina bwa.

questions.question: What does 알빠노 mean in this reply?
questions.explanation: 알빠노 shuts the topic down with indifference — not confusion, and not hurt feelings, just disinterest.

options.text: I don’t know what they said.

dialogue.speaker: 친구
dialogue.korean: 저 둘 매치 뭐야, 실력 차이 하나도 안 나 보여.
dialogue.roman: jeo dul maechi mwoya, sillyeok chai hanado an na boyeo.

questions.question: What does 자강두천 describe here?
questions.explanation: 자강두천 assumes both sides are already strong — the drama is that neither one can pull ahead.

options.text: A match between two evenly matched opponents.

dialogue.speaker: 친구
dialogue.korean: 나 다음 달에 콘서트 가기로 확정됐어!
dialogue.roman: na daeum dare konseoteu gagiro hwakjeongdwaesseo!

questions.question: What is 무야호 expressing here?
questions.explanation: 무야호 doesn’t question or doubt the news — it’s just a loud, joyful reaction, borrowed from a moment that had that same energy.
